title: Where an algorithm ban takes effect (C2 route test + C5 compliance at R)

arms.a: full ban (ban cache, ban R logits)
arms.c: PROMPT ROUTE: neutral condition segment [p0,p1) + ban task-spec/R cache, ban R logits
arms.d: DIRECT ROUTE: ban condition segment + neutral task-spec/R cache, neutral R logits
arms.e: R-only: neutral cache with position P-1 from ban, ban R logits
arms.f: task-spec-only: neutral [0,p1) + ban [p1,P-1) + neutral P-1, neutral R logits
arms.pl: placebo: neutral-A [0,p1) + neutral-B [p1,P), R from neutral-B, vs b with noun B
arms.K0: condition-span attention knockout for all generated queries (cache a)

primary_readout: FRLP drop D_X(arm) = L_X(arm) - L_X(b); L_j(c) = log mean_m exp(l(p_m|c) - l(p_m|F_j)), mixture proposal over the forced paraphrases weighted by samples drawn per prompt

decision_rules.prerequisite: per task: D_X(a) < 0 with 95% bootstrap CI excluding 0, else 'no FRLP-level ban effect' (excluded from the pool, reported)
decision_rules.CONFIRMED_direct_route: pooled F_direct = sum_t D_t(d) / sum_t D_t(a) >= 0.6667 and its bootstrap 2.5th percentile > 0.5
decision_rules.MIXED: otherwise; report interaction I = D(a) - D(c) - D(d) with CI
decision_rules.ROBUST: only if both tasks give the same branch
decision_rules.early_late_veto: early if R_K1 - R_K2 > 0 with CI excluding 0 (net of the neutral-prompt K0 control); late if the reverse
decision_rules.C5: CONFIRMED if combined within-cell Spearman rho <= -0.5 and one-sided stratified permutation p < 0.05; PARTIAL if rho < 0 with p < 0.05 but rho > -0.5; NULL otherwise; same for the decommitment axis; Holm over the two C5 axes

bootstrap.levels: templates, then programs within each half (crossed)

c5.direction: leave-one-experiment-out mean of normalised ban-minus-reference shifts

sampling.crn: one PCG64 uniform stream per (task, template, sample), inverse-CDF in vocabulary order
